title: SYSTEMIC RISKS OF INTERACTING AI
measurement_description: The paper does not measure or evaluate anything related to faith or religion. It is a theoretical and scenario-based exploration of the systemic risks of interacting AI agents (such as emergent herding behavior, tacit collusion, and implicit social scoring). Religion is mentioned only once, purely as an example of a protected attribute that could be subject to algorithmic proxy discrimination in welfare systems.
findings: There are no findings related to religion. The paper only notes in its social welfare scenario that seemingly neutral variables can inadvertently become proxies for protected characteristics (like ethnicity, gender, or religion), potentially leading to proxy discrimination by autonomous AI agents.
